I've been working this land since I was 17. My father taught me, and his father before him. I don't read much but I know this soil. Same wheat-maize rotation every year — that's how everyone does it in Quzhou. My whole 10.1 mu does wheat first, then I turn it to maize after the wheat comes off in June.

**Wheat (planting around October):**
I'll go with the improved wheat variety they sell at the township seed station — same one I've used the past three or four years. Good results, no surprises. Before planting I'll rotary till and mix in compound fertilizer. Then I spread urea again before the cold sets in, and once more at jointing. Three irrigations at least — I always do one right before planting to get moisture deep, one at jointing, one when heads come out. If summer is late I'll add a fourth. Sprays: one for aphids and rust in spring, one herbicide pass in winter. I expect maybe 450 jin per mu — that's been typical for me.

**Maize (planting late June after wheat harvest):**
I push fast after wheat harvest — don't want to lose days. I use hybrid maize seed, same brand as the past two years. Yields were decent. I rotary till once to break up the stubble. Apply compound fertilizer at planting, then chase with urea when the plants are about knee-high. Irrigate twice — once at planting if dry, once at silking. Maybe a third time if August is brutal. One pesticide spray for corn borer, maybe one more if I see pests. I figure about 550 jin per mu.

My son sends money home so I can afford the inputs I need, but I don't want to waste. I keep doing what's worked.
